instruction: [level:beginner] [topic:ADB] verify a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: pull one Android file to Windows with visible failures.
Steps: enable USB debugging, run `adb devices`, accept the phone prompt, then pull the file.
```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "C:\PhonePulls\batch_00" | Out-Null
adb pull "/sdcard/Download/report.txt" "C:\PhonePulls\batch_00"
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "adb pull failed" }
```
Why: `adb devices` proves the bridge is authorized, and `$LASTEXITCODE` prevents a failed copy from looking successful.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:ADB] explain a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: pull over wireless ADB after USB authorization.
Steps: connect USB once, run `adb tcpip 5555`, find the phone IP, then connect by IP.
```powershell
adb tcpip 5555
adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555
adb pull "/sdcard/Download/report.txt" "C:\PhonePulls\batch_00"
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Error "wireless adb pull failed" }
```
Why: USB is used only to trust the laptop; TCP mode lets ADB work on the same WiFi.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:ADB] verify a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
[level:beginner] [topic:WiFi Direct] set up a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: confirm the Windows laptop can participate in WiFi Direct.
```powershell
netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String "Wi-Fi Direct"
Get-NetAdapter | Sort-Object Status,Name
```
Why: WiFi Direct depends on the wireless driver exposing a virtual adapter; the check tells you if Windows can form a peer link.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:WiFi Direct] debug a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: test a WiFi Direct or hotspot peer path without guessing.
```powershell
$PhoneIp = "192.168.49.2"
Test-Connection $PhoneIp -Count 2
Test-NetConnection $PhoneIp -Port 7000
```
Why: ping proves layer-3 reachability, while `Test-NetConnection` proves the app port is reachable.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:WiFi Direct] set up a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: serve a diagnostic file to the phone over the peer network.
```powershell
$Port = 7000
$Root = "C:\PhoneShare"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Root | Out-Null
python -m http.server $Port --directory $Root
```
Why: a tiny HTTP server removes SMB and pairing variables; if the phone browser opens the URL, the WiFi Direct route works.

instruction: [level:beginner] [topic:Bluetooth PAN] show a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: find the Bluetooth PAN adapter and check whether it has an IP address.
```powershell
Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object Name -like "*Bluetooth*"
ipconfig /all
```
Why: Bluetooth PAN behaves like a slow Ethernet link; it still needs an adapter, address, and route.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:Bluetooth PAN] verify a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: verify a PAN connection after pairing and tethering.
```powershell
$PhoneGateway = "192.168.44.1"
Test-Connection $PhoneGateway -Count 2
route print
```
Why: the gateway ping confirms the phone is the PAN router, and the route table shows whether traffic will use it.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:Bluetooth PAN] show a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: capture useful PAN troubleshooting state for a repeatable report.
```powershell
$Out = "C:\PhoneDiagnostics\bluetooth-pan.txt"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $Out) | Out-Null
Get-NetAdapter | Out-File $Out
ipconfig /all | Out-File $Out -Append
Get-NetRoute | Out-File $Out -Append
```
Why: adapter, address, and route data together show whether the failure is pairing, DHCP, or routing.

instruction: [level:beginner] [topic:Screen Mirroring] automate a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: mirror an Android screen with scrcpy after ADB is authorized.
```powershell
adb devices
scrcpy --max-size 1280 --video-bit-rate 4M
```
Why: scrcpy uses ADB transport, so fixing ADB authorization usually fixes mirroring startup.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:Screen Mirroring] show a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: mirror over WiFi after switching ADB to TCP mode.
```powershell
adb tcpip 5555
adb connect 192.168.1.30:5555
scrcpy --tcpip --video-bit-rate 4M
```
Why: TCP mirroring avoids the cable, but it needs the phone and laptop on a reachable network.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:Screen Mirroring] automate a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
[level:beginner] [topic:File Sharing] recover a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: create a temporary Windows folder that a phone can download from in a browser.
```powershell
$Root = "C:\PhoneDrop00"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Root | Out-Null
python -m http.server 8080 --directory $Root
```
Why: browser-based HTTP avoids account, SMB, and Bluetooth profile issues during first tests.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:File Sharing] automate a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: copy a folder to a shared Windows location with retry behavior.
```batch
robocopy C:\Incoming C:\PhoneDrop00 /E /R:2 /W:3 /NFL /NDL
if errorlevel 8 exit /b %errorlevel%
```
Why: robocopy exit codes below 8 can be normal copy states; 8 or higher means a real failure.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:File Sharing] recover a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: create an SMB share for controlled phone file access on trusted WiFi.
```powershell
$Path = "C:\PhoneDrop00"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Path | Out-Null
New-SmbShare -Name "PhoneDrop00" -Path $Path -ChangeAccess $env:USERNAME
Get-SmbShare -Name "PhoneDrop00"
```
Why: the share name and NTFS permissions both matter; the command makes both explicit.

instruction: [level:beginner] [topic:Troubleshooting] debug a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: reset the most common ADB failure path.
```powershell
adb kill-server
adb start-server
adb devices
```
Why: restarting the server clears stale USB and TCP sessions, then `devices` shows whether the phone is unauthorized or offline.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:Troubleshooting] recover a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: distinguish firewall, routing, and service failures.
```powershell
$PhoneIp = "192.168.1.20"
Test-Connection $PhoneIp -Count 2
Test-NetConnection $PhoneIp -Port 5555
Get-NetFirewallProfile
```
Why: reachability, port state, and firewall profile point to different fixes.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:Troubleshooting] debug a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: produce a compact troubleshooting bundle for phone-laptop networking.
```powershell
$Out = "C:\PhoneDiagnostics\network-bundle.txt"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $Out) | Out-Null
adb devices -l | Out-File $Out
ipconfig /all | Out-File $Out -Append
route print | Out-File $Out -Append
netstat -ano | Out-File $Out -Append
```
Why: this captures USB state, addresses, routes, and listening ports in one reproducible artifact.

instruction: [level:beginner] [topic:Network Basics] explain a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: check whether phone and laptop are on the same IPv4 network.
```powershell
ipconfig
Get-NetIPConfiguration | Select-Object InterfaceAlias,IPv4Address,IPv4DefaultGateway
```
Why: devices on the same subnet can usually talk directly; different subnets may need routing or hotspot mode.

instruction: [level:intermediate] [topic:Network Basics] set up a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: trace the path from laptop to phone.
```powershell
Test-Connection 192.168.0.20 -Count 3
tracert 192.168.0.20
arp -a | Select-String "192.168.0.20"
```
Why: ping, route hops, and ARP together show whether packets reach the local network and resolve the phone.

instruction: [level:advanced] [topic:Network Basics] explain a Windows 11 phone-to-laptop networking task with real commands and explain why. Scenario 0.
output:
Goal: inspect Windows network selection when several links are active.
```powershell
Get-NetIPInterface | Sort-Object InterfaceMetric | Select-Object InterfaceAlias,AddressFamily,InterfaceMetric
Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 | Sort-Object RouteMetric | Select-Object -First 10
```
Why: Windows picks lower metric routes first, so WiFi, PAN, and virtual adapters can change where traffic goes.
